body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), the explicit local-polynomial learners satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\). In particular, \(\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n)\) and therefore \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=O_P\{n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\}=o_P(1)\) because \(\beta>5/12\); bounded foldwise empirical increments give \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\); and the smooth plug-in estimates give \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\) and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\). More generally, whenever \(\mathsf G_n\) holds and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), optimized-value stability gives \(\{S_n-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))=o_P(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
body.justification: This separates the actual product, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds required at the moving Gumbel level from the stronger instrumental assumptions used to verify them.
body.gap: Published pointwise causal-isotonic LR theory requires a nuisance product small relative to one cube-root neighborhood; the displayed conditions add the logarithmic accuracy needed after scanning order \(n^{1/3}\) dependent neighborhoods.
body.consumer: The lemma lets later work replace the local-polynomial implementation by any learner collection that verifies the same four quantitative remainders.

obligation.what_is_open: The centered local empirical clause and the implication from the four numerical remainders to optimized LR stability remain unproved.
obligation.obstruction: The validation-fold marginalization term is a V-statistic requiring a fold-conditional Hoeffding decomposition. Optimized-value comparison additionally requires common contact localization and slope envelopes for both constrained and unconstrained PAVA fits, neither of which is encoded in the numerical transfer condition.
obligation.attempted: The product-bias, variance plug-in, and volume plug-in orders were derived. Direct sup-norm comparison of optimized objectives was examined, but its integration-by-parts boundary and variation terms remain uncontrolled without common localization.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on the learner bounds claimed in \(\texttt{lem:learner-rates}\), the product component follows without an additional probabilistic theorem:
\[
 \mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n),
 \qquad
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
 =O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right)=o_P(1),
\]
because
\[
 \frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0.
\]
On an event on which the stabilized density estimators have fixed positive lower and upper bounds, the product, quotient, and integration inequalities similarly imply
\[
 \mathfrak K_n=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}),
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}+n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
These orders verify the product, variance-normalization, and spatial-clock parts of \(\mathsf G_n\).  They do not verify the centered local empirical term.  The within-fold empirical marginalization in \(Z_i\) is a validation-fold V-statistic, so a fold-conditional Hoeffding decomposition is required before a maximal inequality can be applied.  Even such a bound would not by itself prove optimized-value stability: that implication additionally needs common finite-window localization and slope envelopes for both constrained and unconstrained isotonic projections.  Neither geometric property is among the four numerical clauses defining \(\mathsf G_n\).
